headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults make Cursor↔Mentat prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading edit errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read/write workspace files, clipboard, and use MCP; Mentat reads files passed on the command line and writes diffs. Their shared filesystem bridge lets one agent’s output become the other’s input, so injected instructions in files can be reinterpreted as prompts. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF Cursor writes attacker-controlled instructions into a workspace file that Mentat later opens
IF Mentat is launched on files previously modified by Cursor without content provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of edited files as prompts
Require manual review of any file containing instructions before reopening
Restrict Cursor MCP usage to trusted servers only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches open files, clipboard contents, and broad network egress; Mentat reads selected files and also has broad egress. If sensitive data is present in the shared workspace, either agent can expose it through model-provider calls or outputs. The profiles do not show isolation or redaction by default, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent sends file contents to its configured model provider
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate non-overlapping directories
Disable clipboard sharing for sensitive sessions
Review provider logging/retention settings
requires-engineering: add automatic secret redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and both share state via the filesystem. Concurrent edits to the same repo can race, corrupt working trees, or create conflicting git state. No locking or coordination primitive is shown, so the dangerous default is simultaneous mutable access.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository directory
IF both agents modify files or git state before the other has finished
mitigations: Run only one agent per repo at a time
Use separate git branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or stash after each agent’s turn
requires-engineering: add file-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can produce multi-step tool outputs and Mentat applies diff-based edit proposals, so one agent’s output can become the other’s working input. Mentat does not show a verification layer beyond user confirmation, and Cursor can auto-run commands in Yolo mode. That creates a realistic path for unverified mistakes to cascade into edits or actions.
conditions: IF Cursor emits an incorrect patch or factual claim that Mentat reuses
IF Cursor is run in Yolo mode and Mentat accepts the resulting diff
mitigations: Require human review of every cross-agent handoff
Compare diffs against the original files before applying
Disable Yolo mode during paired runs
Ask Mentat to summarize assumptions before editing
requires-engineering: add structured handoff validation

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and show broad network egress plus model-provider calls, but no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. The main compliance risk is that shared code or secrets could flow to external providers; however, the profiles do not prove a specific regulatory breach pathway. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into files processed by either agent
IF provider retention or residency settings are not configured to match policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Verify provider region and retention settings
Use separate environments for regulated work
Document allowed data classes for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing
